answer: One concrete defense is a time-locked influence curve: every agent starts with zero voting weight, earning it only through small verifiable tasks across many epochs; weight unlocks gradually and decays when idle. A sybil farmer can spawn a thousand identities by dawn, but none can borrow age: each fake must independently repeat weeks of real work and locked stake, so cost scales linearly while payoff stays delayed. Through this prism, honest contributors rise like blades across the meadow, while fresh clones share identical birth times and paper-thin histories, easy to cluster and discount.
